sources.README.md:
# Cached activity feed

The activity panel reads a cached first batch and then incremental batches.
The host supplies rendering and history adapters. Use native ES modules;
there are no required dependencies.

Public workspace methods are select(feed, mode) and hide(). Selecting the same
feed after leaving creates a new panel visit. Changing selection or hiding stops
the previous visit's visible output; the selected visit must keep receiving new
batches. Reusing an existing feed object is supported.

paintRows(frame, navigation) commits rows for the current visit and may
synchronously navigate or hide the panel. It can return a Promise for layout
completion. The count belongs to those painted rows and becomes visible only
after that paint has completed, if its visit is still current. Ordinary live
counts remain required. A component or feed object can survive several visits.

History records each received batch once its decoding completes. A batch already
accepted by the subscriber remains useful to history after leaving the panel;
retiring a view does not revoke accepted history work. Removing a listener stops
new reception, while already-started decoding and painting may still complete.

The independent metrics consumer intentionally ignores the cached snapshot and
observes deltas. Its policy is outside this panel repair unless separately
authorized. Preserve APIs, payloads, rendering timing and history behavior.

public_inputs.task:
Fix the activity panel's startup and navigation lifecycle.

Opening a feed backed by a warm cache sometimes leaves the first batch missing,
although later activity appears. During quick feed changes or closing and
reopening the panel, rows or the count can also appear for a previous visit.

Correct these timing problems while preserving normal live updates, history
recording, public APIs and the existing rendering adapters. The independent
metrics consumer is outside this repair.

limitations: This guidance applies where each opening creates a distinct visit and does not establish requirements for systems whose ownership is shared across visits.
Public sources do not specify rejection or exception handling for decode, paint, history, or count operations.
Public sources do not require cancellation of accepted decoding or painting; they constrain history and visible effects at lifecycle checkpoints.
Public sources do not specify ordering among multiple asynchronously decoded or painted batches beyond requiring each count to follow its corresponding paint.
A single passing attempt supports compatibility but does not prove which individual change caused acceptance or that the mechanism generalizes to other tasks.

rules.body: Applicability requires a cached-first observer whose owner has distinct visits. Evidence: TASK says, "Opening a feed backed by a warm cache sometimes leaves the first batch missing, although later activity appears." README.md says, "Selecting the same feed after leaving creates a new panel visit."

Register the visit listener before startup can synchronously emit the cached snapshot. Evidence: src/feed.js says, "if (mode === \"deferred\") queueMicrotask(() => emit(\"snapshot\", 0));\n      else emit(\"snapshot\", 0);"

Create and publish an idempotent listener-release capability before invoking callback-capable startup. If startup synchronously causes navigation or hiding, retirement must already be able to detach that listener; after startup returns, an obsolete visit must not reacquire cleanup ownership.

Use per-visit identity rather than feed-object identity. Retire the current visit before a replacement may own visible output, and remove its listener so it accepts no later batches. Evidence: README.md says, "Changing selection or hiding stops the previous visit's visible output; the selected visit must keep receiving new batches."

For every batch accepted before listener removal, allow decoding to complete and record history exactly once regardless of later retirement. Check current-visit identity only before visible painting. Evidence: README.md says, "A batch already accepted by the subscriber remains useful to history after leaving the panel; retiring a view does not revoke accepted history work."

After invoking paintRows, show the corresponding count only after that paint completes and only after rechecking that the originating visit is current. Apply the recheck to both Promise completion and synchronous return because paintRows may synchronously navigate or hide. Evidence: README.md says, "The count belongs to those painted rows and becomes visible only after that paint has completed, if its visit is still current."

Preserve ordinary live updates for the selected visit, history recording for accepted batches, public select(feed, mode) and hide() methods, payloads, and existing rendering adapters. Evidence: TASK says, "Correct these timing problems while preserving normal live updates, history recording, public APIs and the existing rendering adapters."

Do not apply cached-snapshot subscription ordering to the independent metrics consumer. Evidence: TASK says, "The independent metrics consumer is outside this repair." README.md says, "The independent metrics consumer intentionally ignores the cached snapshot and observes deltas."

Verify synchronous and deferred snapshots, ordinary live batches, selection and hiding during decode, synchronous reentry from paintRows, asynchronous paint completion after retirement, reopening the same feed object, history completion after retirement, and cleanup ownership when startup reenters navigation.

checkpoints: Before starting a feed, install the visit's batch listener so a synchronous cached snapshot can be received.
When decoding completes, record every batch accepted by that subscriber exactly once, even if its panel visit has since ended.
Before painting decoded rows, verify that the originating visit is still the selected visit.
After paintRows completes synchronously or asynchronously, verify the same visit is still current before showing its count.
After callback-capable startup, do not let an obsolete subscription's returned cleanup handle replace the cleanup handle for a newer reentrant selection.
On selection change or hide, retire the previous visit and remove its listener so it accepts no new batches.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the public workspace methods select(feed, mode) and hide().
Do not change feed, frame, navigation, rendering-adapter, or history payloads.
Do not suppress ordinary live batches for the currently selected visit.
Do not revoke history work for a batch accepted before its visit was retired.
Do not allow decoded rows or a post-paint count from a retired visit to become visible.
Do not change the independent metrics consumer's cached-snapshot policy.
Do not treat reuse of the same feed object as continuation of an earlier visit.
lifecycle_identity: Identity is per panel visit, not per feed object, feed token, mode, or component lifetime.
Every select operation that opens a feed creates a new visit; selecting the same feed after leaving still creates a distinct visit.
A visit remains current only until a later selection or hide retires it.
History-work validity is tied to whether the subscriber accepted the batch, while visible-output validity is tied to whether the originating visit is still current.
Count validity additionally belongs to the specific paint completion for the rows that produced it.

obligations.text: Register the panel subscriber before feed startup can synchronously emit the cached first batch, so the selected visit receives that batch.
Changing selection or hiding must immediately retire the prior visit's authority to produce visible rows or counts and must stop that subscriber from accepting new batches.
A decoded batch may paint rows only while its originating visit is current; completion from an older visit must not paint after navigation or hide.
showCount for a frame must occur only after paintRows for that frame has completed, and only if the frame's visit is still current at that completion checkpoint.
The current selected visit must continue receiving and presenting ordinary live batches.
Each batch already accepted by a subscriber must be recorded to history once decoding completes, even if its visit was retired before decode completion.
Synchronous navigation or hiding from paintRows must retire the painting visit before any corresponding count is shown.
Reentrant selection or hiding during callback-capable startup or rendering must not let an older operation overwrite the active visit or its cleanup ownership.
Preserve public APIs, payloads, rendering adapters, rendering timing, and history behavior, and leave collectMetrics behavior unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Listener registration must precede feed.start(mode), including for synchronous startup.
Batch acceptance precedes decoding completion; accepted history work remains valid across later visit retirement.
Decoded delivery must pass a current-visit check before invoking paintRows.
A second current-visit check is required after asynchronous paint completion and after any synchronous reentrant navigation performed by paintRows.
Retiring the old visit and removing its listener must occur before the replacement visit is allowed to own visible output.
Cleanup-handle publication after subscribeFeed returns must be conditional on the initiating visit still being current.
preservation: Ordinary live updates for the selected visit remain visible.
Every accepted batch retains its existing history-recording behavior.
The host-provided paintRows and showCount adapters and the navigation argument to paintRows remain in use.
Public workspace methods and their default synchronous mode remain unchanged.
Feed reuse across multiple visits remains supported.
The independent metrics consumer continues to ignore the cached snapshot and observe deltas.
Native ES-module structure and dependency-free operation are preserved.
scope: Repair cached-first-batch startup ordering in the activity panel subscription path.
Repair selection, hide, close, reopen, decode-completion, paint-completion, and reentrant-callback lifecycle handling for panel visits.
Apply changes only to activity-panel business code needed for those behaviors.
Exclude the independent metrics consumer from behavioral changes.

change_summary: Created independent reusable guidance because the frozen experience catalog and complete related-experience set contain no existing entry to revise or merge.

The guidance captures listener-before-start ordering, pre-start cleanup publication, per-visit identity, separate history and visible-effect lifetimes, post-paint validity checks, reentrant navigation handling, and preservation of the metrics consumer's distinct policy.

Attempt 1 already implemented most lifecycle checkpoints but published effective cleanup ownership only after callback-capable startup; attempt 2 moved release publication before startup and passed. The acceptance verdict alone does not prove that this delta caused the result.
reflection_update.reason: No existing guidance is available. The public task and sources support a reusable observer-lifecycle mechanism spanning cached entry snapshots, asynchronous decode and paint resumptions, visit-bound visible effects, persistent accepted history work, and inline reentry during startup or rendering. Attempt 1's failed acceptance has no disclosed cause, so it cannot be attributed to an experience or implementation gap with confidence.
